newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - June 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuter has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Beijing announced the name list of China's delegation to Hong Kong's handover celebration, which included the widow of the late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

-- The People's Liberation Army Hong Kong garrison major-general Zhou Borong, who reportedly complained about being stopped by Hong Kong customs officers when crossing the border without valid travel documents, paid a visit to the Customs headquarters but refused to comment on the earlier reports.
-- APPLE DAILY -- The Democratic Party will take action in the Legislative Council after midnight on July 1 to express its stance of "supporting the handover and fighting for democracy".

-- One third of people surveyed were worried of worsening corruption after the handover and political instability. An analyst said corruption would be the biggest problem for Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa and his new government.
-- SING TAO -- Beijing will crackdown on illegal promotional activities, focusing on groups which use marketing training as a way to spread superstitious thinking and gangster culture.

-- Sources said Beijing was surprised that the popularity and authority of Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui dropped sharply in the past year, and believed Lee will switch attention to mainland-Taiwan relations to bring back his popularity.

-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Sources said China Everbright-IHD's acquisition of a stake in a China commercial bank was a special case. No other commercial banks could be injected into Hong Kong listed companies or be listed in here in the near future.
-- A securities analyst predicted that capital from China will continue to flow into the territory after the handover and be invested in red chip shares.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The recent surge in the share prices of red chip companies brought huge profit to executives of these Chnna-backed companies. But sources said the Chinese government is studying how to make regulations so that the major chunk of the profit will be handed to the state.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Since the 1980s, more than 8,000 highrises with more than 20 floors have been built in China, thought to be a record. The tallest will be an 88-storey financial centre in Shanghai's Pudong district scheduled for completion in 1998.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- A source familiar with Hong Kong's air services agreements said close scrutiny by Beijing of the territory's air service agreements had delayed the development of air links between Hong Kong and the rest of the world.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Uncertainty over future government policy towards the property sector was threatening to undermine interest in property developments being offered by developers in the next two weeks.
